However, in addition to laws adopted by the state, the advertising industry has also promoted and developed extensive self-regulation. For instance, in the US, in 2006, the FTC adopted its Endorsement Guides [7] applicable to social media, which were updated in 2022 to include more specific references to influencer marketing; in the Netherlands, the Stichting Reclame Code adopted a Social Media Advertising Code, updated in 2022 to the Social Media and Influencer Marketing Advertising Code [8]. Similarly, Brazil adopted its Digital Influencer Advertising Guidelines in 2021 [9].

While codes of conduct and guidelines feature detailed standards (e.g., what hashtags to use for disclosure and influencer definitions), they often do not have a mandatory status. Consequently, enforcing these  rules  in  practice  is  difficult,  as  additional  administrative  and judicial actions are necessary.

In this sense, Balenciaga's fashion is not contemporary at all; rather, Gvasalia resuscitates fashion scenes from his past and mixes them with references to the work of 1990s anti-fashion designers like Martin Margiela. Gvasalia has turned Balenciaga into a fashion label that is based largely on internet hype and has turned a Parisian fashion house into meme fashion or Post-Internet fashion, making enormous profits from garments that are essentially Balenciaga merchandise sold at very high prices. The latest provocation by the brand is a skirt made out of a terry cloth towel sold at a price of 695 €. 1 The lack of refinement and creativity in Balenciaga garments and designs are compensated for by a skillful use of the aesthetics of contemporary dystopias. As observed above, there is an apparent dearth of scholarship regarding work uniforms in private-as opposed to institutional or governmental-service organizations,  and  luxury  services  in  particular.  The  one  exception  is  designer  airline uniforms [2, 30, 31]. A recent publication by Akou [5] examines public and private service sector work uniform cases in the USA, but does not cover luxury branded services specifically. Furthermore, uniforms are frequently discussed in fashion literature as sources of inspiration for fashion designers, or as subversive items of subculture fashion [32, 33]. But the influence contemporary fashions may have on uniform creation is not considered. This is likely because-as noted by scholarswork uniforms in general tend to be resistant to change, may be subject to industry norms and regulations, and are mass-manufactured by suppliers which operate outside the 'fashion system' [34]. However, these conditions only partially apply to bespoke corporate uniforms designed ad-hoc for luxury brands by highly specialized suppliers. In fact, as suggested in the introduction, the level of customization these projects require most likely implies the activation of creative processes that are similar, if not identical, to fashion design inspiration, research, and development [35]. To the author's best knowledge, however, such processes have not heretofore been investigated.

The	accounts	of	its	pilot programs	describe	powerful	examples	of	surveillance	capitalism's	economies	of action and the intricate construction of superscale means of behavior modification.	The	aim	is	the	automation	of	society	through	tuning,	herding,	and conditioning	people	to	produce	preselected	behaviors	judged	as	desirable	by	the state	 and	 thus	 able	 to	 'preempt	 instability,'	 as	 one	 strategic	 studies	 expert	 put it.
